r0-context.title: Load baseline context
r0-context.imperative: Read CREW_CONTEXT.md, engine-config.json, the handoff, the diff, and the change. Record pass when loaded.
r0-context.finding: Read CREW_CONTEXT.md, engine-config.json, handoff, utilization.py, test_utilization.py, simplification_limits.py. Inherited rules map directly to handoff constraints.

r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: Module delivers UTILIZATION_LEVELS, frozen ResourcePlan, resolve_resource_plan, init_worker, run_jobs with in-process short-circuit at 1 worker and input-order reassembly. 25 tests + psutil dep. Built test-first per docstrings. All close criteria met (verified individually below).

r2-scope.title: Scope drift
r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect specific exclusions? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r2-scope.finding: git status: only pyproject.toml modified (+psutil>=5.9.0), plus new src/utils/utilization.py and tests/unit/test_utilization.py. No gold_cycle/sampled_backtest/run.py/scripts touched. No new CLI/config knob. Module not yet wired into callers (correct for a shared-core gate). .agent-work/ is workflow state (excluded).

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Re-ran myself: pytest tests/unit/test_utilization.py -> 25 passed; simplification_limits --paths -> PASS (2 files). simplification_limits enforces real metrics (file<1000, func<100, CC<20), so non-vacuous. Independently re-derived invariant/mapping/fallback/fail_fast.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: All inherited CREW_CONTEXT rules satisfied; per-rule detail recorded in q-* checks below.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: New leaf utility under src/utils/; no architecture-baseline contract changed, no doc/schema divergence. Adds a dependency (psutil) which is a normal additive change. No reconciliation needed.

q-fagnostic.title: F1-agnostic module
q-fagnostic.imperative: No DB/calendar/evo/F1 imports or concepts in module.
q-fagnostic.finding: Imports are stdlib (logging,math,os,concurrent.futures,dataclasses,typing) + psutil only. grep for f1/calendar/evo/database/fastf1/circuit/DriverFeatures: matches only in the docstring declaring agnosticism. No domain concepts.

q-nostate.title: No mutable module-level state
q-nostate.imperative: No mutable module-level runtime state or impure caches.
q-nostate.finding: Module-level names: UTILIZATION_LEVELS/_PRIORITIES (tuples), _LEVEL_PLANS (constant lookup dict), _JOB_REPR_LIMIT (int), logger. Verified _LEVEL_PLANS unchanged after a clamp-triggering resolve. No caches. Worker/thread counts flow through function scope + frozen ResourcePlan.

q-logging.title: Logging not print
q-logging.finding: logger=logging.getLogger(__name__) at module top; logger.info/.debug used throughout. grep print( : no matches.

q-validation.title: Validation messages
q-validation.imperative: Validation messages name field, expectation, actual.
q-validation.finding: Invalid level: 'level must be one of (...), got turbo' names field+expected-set+actual. mem<=0: 'mem_per_worker_gb must be > 0, got 0' names field+expectation+actual.

q-clamp.title: cores=1 thread clamp inert at cores>=2
q-clamp.imperative: Commander-sanctioned clamp keeps workers*threads<=cores at cores=1; zero effect at cores>=2.
q-clamp.finding: utilization.py:146-157 clamps threads to max(1,cores//n_workers). Verified: cores=1 balanced -> (1,1) [nominal (1,2) would violate]; cores>=2 balanced keeps threads=2 across cores 2..16 (clamp inert). Commander-sanctioned; correct and zero effect at cores>=2.

q-mapping.title: Level->plan mapping at cores=8
q-mapping.finding: cores=8: background=(1,1,below_normal), balanced=(4,2,normal), max=(7,1,normal). Matches criterion exactly (tests + my direct re-derivation).

q-invariant.title: workers*threads<=cores invariant
q-invariant.imperative: Holds every level/core count including cores=1.
q-invariant.finding: Re-derived n_workers*threads<=cores AND n_workers>=1 AND threads>=1 for every level at cores 1..16, including cores=1. Holds everywhere.

q-ramcap.title: RAM cap binds and logs once
q-ramcap.imperative: Cap lowers n_workers, logs once, never below 1.
q-ramcap.finding: available_mem_gb=2,mem_per_worker_gb=1,max(8c) -> 2 workers; log names before(7)/after(2)+mem reason, emitted only when capped (utilization.py:96-104). available=0.1 -> floor to 1 (never <1). Tests cover both.

q-fallback.title: physical_cores=None fallback
q-fallback.imperative: Falls back to psutil.cpu_count(logical=False) or os.cpu_count() or 1.
q-fallback.finding: _detect_physical_cores is exactly 'psutil.cpu_count(logical=False) or os.cpu_count() or 1'. Tests monkeypatch psutil->6 (workers=5 for max) and psutil->None+os->4 (workers=2 balanced), covering the chain's first two rungs.

q-order.title: Input-order reassembly multi-worker
q-order.imperative: Results reassembled in input order despite inverted completion order.
q-order.finding: _run_in_pool places results at submission index (results[index]=...), so input order is independent of completion. Test _sleep_then_index sleeps 0.02*(5-job) so completion order is reversed (4,3,2,1,0) yet asserts [0,1,2,3,4]. Genuinely exercises reassembly.

q-inprocess.title: n_workers==1 in-process, no pool
q-inprocess.imperative: Single worker takes in-process path; ProcessPoolExecutor never constructed.
q-inprocess.finding: run_jobs: plan.n_workers<=1 returns _run_in_process (no pool). Test monkeypatches utilization.ProcessPoolExecutor to _ExplodingPool (raises on construct); single-worker run returns [1,4,9,16] without triggering it. _run_in_pool references module-global name so the guard is effective -> non-vacuous.

q-failfast.title: fail_fast wraps + closes pool
q-failfast.imperative: First error wrapped with job identity; pool closed; no deadlock/orphan.
q-failfast.finding: fail_fast=True wraps first error as JobExecutionError naming index+truncated repr, raised inside the 'with' so pool __exit__ runs (shutdown wait=True). Probe with slow siblings: raised JobExecutionError containing 'index 0', returned in ~4.5s (waited for siblings; no deadlock/orphan). Criterion (wrapped identity + pool closed) met. Note: waits for in-flight siblings rather than cancelling -- safe, observation only.

q-notorch.title: Imports without torch
q-notorch.imperative: Module imports cleanly without torch; torch import lazy/guarded in init_worker.
q-notorch.finding: torch import is inside init_worker, guarded by try/except. Verified: forcing sys.modules['torch']=None still imports the module cleanly. Test also confirms init_worker tolerates ImportError on torch.

q-initworker.title: init_worker module-level picklable
q-initworker.finding: init_worker is a module-level def, used as ProcessPoolExecutor(initializer=init_worker, initargs=...). Test asserts utilization.init_worker is the imported symbol (module-level -> picklable under spawn).

q-nonvacuous.title: Tests non-vacuous
q-nonvacuous.imperative: Tests genuinely assert contracts (ordering inverted, exploding-pool guard, etc.), not trivially.
q-nonvacuous.finding: Spot-checked: ordering test inverts completion order; in-process test uses an exploding-pool sentinel; fail_fast asserts job identity in message; module-level workers (no lambdas/closures) for real spawn. RAM/fallback tests assert specific worker counts. Not trivially true.

consolidation.summary: G1 shared utilization core: all 21 checks pass. Contracts independently re-verified (mapping, invariant at cores 1..16, RAM cap, core-fallback chain, input-order reassembly, in-process short-circuit with no pool, fail_fast wrapped+pool-closed, torchless import, picklable init_worker). Scope clean (only the 3 allowed files). Tests non-vacuous. No blockers.
